summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 16th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, managed with anti-emetics. Methotrexate levels cleared appropriately, reaching below 0.2 by discharge, with no renal toxicity. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation. An MRI confirmed stable lymphoma without new lesions. Due to a recent ulcerative colitis flare with hematochezia, oral mesalamine was switched to rectal suppositories to avoid interference with methotrexate excretion. Aspirin was held during admission for the same reason and was restarted at discharge. She remained emotionally stable, denied depression or suicidal ideation, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up instructions.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
